exact_statement_tex: \label{thm:finite-descent} Let $A$ be a semilocal noetherian ring, $\mathfrak m=\operatorname{rad}A$, and $A'$ a finite $A$-algebra. Put $A_n=A/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$, $A'_n=A'\otimes_AA_n$, and \[ B=H^0(A'/A),\qquad B^{(n)}=H^0(A'_n/A_n), \] where $H^0$ is the equalizer of the two maps to the tensor square. For any fixed integer $r\geq1$, the following three conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*] \item $H^1(A'_n/A_n,\mathbf G_a)=0$ for every $n$; \item $H^1(A'_n/A_n,\GL_r)=\{1\}$ for every $n$; \item $\Spec A'_n\to\Spec B^{(n)}$ is effective descent for all flat quasi-coherent modules for every $n$. \end{enumerate} Here $H^1$ denotes Amitsur cohomology, or its matrix-cocycle pointed set. If these conditions hold, then they hold for every finite $r$; moreover \[ H^1(A'/A,\mathbf G_a)=0,\qquad H^1(A'/A,\GL_r)=\{1\}\quad(r\geq1), \] and $\Spec A'\to\Spec B$ is effective descent for finite flat modules. If $A$ is Artinian, this map and its base change by every flat $B$-scheme are effective descent for all flat quasi-coherent modules, with no bound on rank.

The filtration is intrinsic to the given torsor action.

exact_statement_tex: \label{rem:characteristic-two-ample-residual} Suppose that $Y$ is merely ample, with the same characteristic-two equality and torsion hypotheses, and additionally suppose that $X$ has a purely inseparable ruled rational cover of degree two. If the resulting ruling curve $C$ has positive genus, the proof above still gives \[ g(C)=1,\qquad \chi(\OO_X)=K_X^2=c_2(X)=0,\qquad b_1(X)=b_2(X)=2. \] The general-fibre identities give a positive even integer $b=Y\cdot F$. Equation~\eqref{eq:characteristic-two-canonical-square}, before its strict inequality, then forces $b=2$ and $p_a(F)=1$. Moreover, $Y\to B=C^{(2)}$ is separable of degree two. Its degree is $Y\cdot F=2$; if it were inseparable, it would be a relative Frobenius followed by an isomorphism and would preserve genus. That would give $g(Y)=1$, contrary to $g(Y)=Y^2+1\geq2$. Thus the purely inseparable multisection obstruction in Proposition~\ref{prop:quasielliptic-multisection} does not already exclude this configuration. The genus-zero branch for merely ample $Y$ satisfies the necessary numerical conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:rational-normalization-canonical}. The present proposition concerns the function field of the normalized cover and does not extend a chosen rational ruling map over every point of that cover. It supplies no existence example for the Picard kernel, and does not settle the higher-conductor or strict-inequality cases.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:residual-adjoint} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral very ample divisor, and let $s$ be its canonical section. Suppose that a nonzero closed global one-form $\omega$ vanishes along $Y$. Let $m$ be its exact order along $Y$, and let $Z$ be the divisorial zero part, with multiplicities, of $\theta=\omega/s^m\in H^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k}(-mY))$. Then $m=pa$ for an integer $a\geq1$, $Y$ is not a component of $Z$, and \[ 0\leq Z\cdot Y\leq 2g(Y)-2-mY^2. \] The divisor \[ A=K_X-(m-2)Y-Z \] is nef and big, with $A^2>0$. More precisely, the linear system \[ W_K=\{d((u/s)\omega):u\in H^0(X,\OO_X(Y))\} \subset H^0(X,\omega_X) \] has exact fixed divisor $(m-2)Y+Z$ and two-dimensional image. Its residual system has no fixed curve, and on a dense open of $Y$ its rational map is the given hyperplane embedding. The map $u\mapsto d((u/s)\omega)$ has kernel $ks$. In particular, \begin{align*} h^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k})&\geq h^0(X,\OO_X(Y)),\\ \operatorname{rank}\bigl[d:H^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k})\to H^0(X,\omega_X)\bigr]&\geq h^0(X,\OO_X(Y))-1,\\ p_g(X)&\geq h^0(X,\OO_X(Y))-1. \end{align*} Both $K_X-(m-2)Y$ and $K_X-(p-2)Y$ are big, and the canonical map of $X$ has two-dimensional image.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:odd-higher-conductor-equality} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$, let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral very ample curve, and let $M$ be a nontrivial line bundle of order $p$ whose restriction to $Y$ is trivial. Exactly the following three rows can survive the canonical divisibility, genus-change and slope bounds: \begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-conductor-three-genera} \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \ell&\text{range of }a&g&\text{divisibility}\\ \hline 1&a\geq5\text{ odd}&(a+1)/2&p-1\mid a+1\\ 2&a\geq7&a&p-1\mid2a\\ 3&a\geq21\text{ odd}&(3a-1)/2&p-1\mid3a-1 \end{array} \end{equation} The second and third rows require a nonhyperelliptic fibration. Every case satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-conductor-characteristic-bound} p\leq2a+1. \end{equation} The rows describe necessary numerical conditions and do not assert the existence of equality cases.

exact_statement_tex: [Curve-pullback excess bound] \label{prop:boundary-curve-pullback-excess} Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$, let $X$ be a normal integral projective surface, and let $C\subset X$ be a smooth integral effective Cartier divisor contained in the smooth locus, with $d=C^2>0$. Let $M\ne\OO_X$ have order $p$ and be trivial on $C$. Suppose its logarithmic form $\omega$ has exact order $pa$ along $C$, where $a\geq1$ and $p\nmid a$, and put \[ \delta=2g(C)-2-pad. \] Suppose that $f:X\to B$ is a nonconstant morphism to a smooth integral projective curve of genus $b\geq1$, and that $M\simeq f^*P$ for a nontrivial order-$p$ line bundle $P$ on $B$. Then $C$ dominates $B$. If $n=\deg(f|_C)$, then $p\mid n$, and there is an integer $0\leq j\leq a-1$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-curve-pullback-bound} \delta\geq\frac{pd}{2(p-1)}+ \frac{n(b-1)}{(p-1)(j+1)} \geq\frac{pd}{2(p-1)}+\frac{n(b-1)}{(p-1)a}. \end{equation} In particular, $b\geq2$ excludes the endpoint $\delta=pd/(2(p-1))$. In characteristic two this reads $\delta\geq d+n(b-1)/a$, and at $a=1$ it reads $\delta\geq d+n(b-1)$. This proposition does not require ampleness of $C$ or a separate N\'eron--Severi divisibility hypothesis.

exact_statement_tex: [Ample wedge restriction] \label{prop:boundary-ample-wedge} Let $X$ be a smooth integral projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, let $C\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor, and put $d=C^2$. Suppose \[ 2g(C)-2=(2a+1)d, \qquad \mathcal T=\omega_C\otimes\OO_C(C)^{-(2a+1)}. \] If a global regular one-form $\beta$ satisfies $\omega\wedge\beta\ne0$, then \begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-ample-wedge-splitting} K_X\sim2aC,\qquad \Omega_X^1\simeq\OO_X(2aC)\oplus\OO_X,\qquad c_2(X)=0,\qquad\mathcal T\simeq\OO_C. \end{equation} Consequently, if $\mathcal T$ is nontrivial, all global regular one-forms are rationally collinear with $\omega$, their pairwise wedge products vanish, and the Albanese map has generic differential rank at most one.

exact_statement_tex: [Scope and comparison] \label{rem:boundary-albanese-scope} The curve-pullback bound uses an existing morphism $X\to B$. The curve-pullback bound does not require a fibration arising from the resolved curve of square zero. Proposition~\ref{prop:boundary-resolved-fibration} does produce a separate fibration on a suitable covering resolution, using actual triviality of its normal line and the moving lemma. The elliptic-base case and the inseparable surface-image case in Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-smallest-albanese-gate} remain unresolved by these arguments. Existence of either configuration remains open. The nonclosed one-forms from Proposition~\ref{prop:residual-adjoint} are compatible with rational collinearity: $d(r\omega)$ can be nonzero although all pairwise wedges vanish. For comparison, Cotner--Zavyalov prove a Lefschetz theorem for finite flat commutative coefficients under a Hodge-equivalence or strongly ample hypothesis \cite[Theorem~3.3.5, pp.~1861--1862]{CotnerZavyalov}. Applied to $\mu_2$ and a strongly ample curve on a surface, it gives injectivity of restriction on order-two line bundles. Strong ampleness is an additional hypothesis; their Example~3.3.6 concerns failure for $\alpha_p$ and does not provide an order-two line-bundle example. Our bound instead retains $\deg\omega_{B'}$ in \eqref{eq:boundary-curve-pullback-conormal}. The remaining inseparable Albanese case belongs to an established foliation setting: Conti describes the canonical inseparable degree-two factorization for a characteristic-two surface whose Albanese image is a surface and whose Albanese map is inseparable \cite[Lemma~2.22 and Remark~2.23, p.~13]{ContiPositiveSeveriComparison}. That description does not itself exclude the endpoint here.

exact_statement_tex: [Global structure at the smallest endpoint] \label{thm:smallest-endpoint-global-structure} Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic two, let $X$ be a smooth integral projective surface, and let $C\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor. Put $d=C^2$ and $N=\OO_C(C)$. Let $M\ne\OO_X$ have exact order two and satisfy $M|_C\simeq\OO_C$. Suppose that $M$ has a square root $L$, that its logarithmic form $\omega$ has exact order two along $C$, and that \[ 2g(C)-2=3d. \] The square-root condition is equivalent to $[M]\in2\operatorname{NS}(X)$. Let $\tau:W\to X$ be the $\mu_2$-torsor of $M$, let $n:V\to W$ be its normalization, put $\pi=\tau n$ and $B=\pi^*C$, and write $\mathfrak c\subset\OO_V$ for the conductor. Then the following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The integer $d$ is even and $\mathcal T=\omega_C\otimes N^{-3}$ has exact order two. The surface $V$ is smooth along $B$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-conductor} \mathfrak c=\OO_V(-B),\qquad \omega_V\simeq\pi^*\bigl(\omega_X(-C)\bigr). \end{equation} In particular, $V$ is Gorenstein. exact_statement_tex: [Exact height and ramification] \label{prop:elliptic-endpoint-height} Let $X$ be a smooth integral projective surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic two, and let $C\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor with $d=C^2$. There is a factorization \begin{equation}\label{eq:elliptic-endpoint-factorization} f|_C=r\circ h,\qquad h:C\longrightarrow E_1, \end{equation} where $h$ is separable of degree $n/2\geq2$. Thus the inseparable degree of $f|_C$ is exactly two and $n\geq4$. The ramification divisor $R_h$, with its different multiplicities, satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:elliptic-endpoint-ramification} \deg R_h=3d,\qquad \operatorname{Supp}R_h\cap\operatorname{Supp}Z=\varnothing. \end{equation} In particular $h$ is unramified at every point of $\operatorname{Supp}Z$.

exact_statement_tex: [The canonical quotient and its Albanese variety] \label{prop:smallest-endpoint-albanese-quotient} The Albanese differential has generic rank exactly one, and \[ T_{X/A}=\mathcal F. \] Let $q:X\to Y$ be the quotient by this foliation and write $\alpha=hq$. exact_statement_tex: [The image divisor on an abelian surface] \label{prop:smallest-endpoint-albanese-surface-defect} Suppose $q_A=2$ and put $D_A=\alpha(C)\subset A$ with its reduced integral structure. Equality in the defect bound holds exactly when $D'$ is smooth. These are assertions about the image divisor, not a formula for $C^2$.

exact_statement_tex: [The image-curve pattern] \label{rem:smallest-endpoint-albanese-image-pattern} The image-divisor conditions alone are compatible with examples. Take ordinary elliptic curves $E_1,E_2$ and the degree-two $\mu_2$-isogeny \[ \rho=F_{E_1/k}\times1: A'=E_1\times E_2\longrightarrow E_1^{(2)}\times E_2=A. \] Choose a smooth sufficiently ample integral curve $D'\subset A'$ whose projection to $E_2$ has nonzero differential. Such a choice follows from Bertini in a sufficiently ample linear system separating first-order jets: impose at one smooth point a tangent direction not killed by the second projection, and choose a general member smooth elsewhere. The restriction of $\rho$ to $D'$ is radicial and has nonzero differential. It is therefore birational onto its image $D_A$. Its normalization kills the line $P$ defining $\rho$, and the defect equality in \eqref{eq:smallest-endpoint-albanese-surface-defect} holds with $\epsilon=0$. This constructs only the image-curve behavior. Taking $X=A'$ would make $\rho^*P$ trivial, and $\rho$ would not be the Albanese map of $A'$. It is not a construction of a surface satisfying the endpoint hypotheses. The existence or exclusion of the full inseparable Albanese endpoint configuration remains open.

exact_statement_tex: [The canonical interval, Stein defect and image divisor] \label{thm:smallest-endpoint-strict-canonical} Under these hypotheses, \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-interval} 2d<K_X^2<3d,\qquad 1\le c_2(X)\le d-1. \end{equation} Write the Stein factorization of $\alpha$ as \[ X\xrightarrow{\,r\,}X_0\xrightarrow{\,a_0\,}A. \] Then $X_0$ is normal and Gorenstein, $a_0$ is a finite flat double cover, and $r$ is proper birational. The quotient $Q=a_{0*}\OO_{X_0}/\OO_A$ is invertible. Set \[ \mathcal L=Q^{-1},\qquad t=\operatorname{length}(R^1r_*\OO_X),\qquad D=K_X-r^*K_{X_0}, \] using compatible canonical divisors. The sheaf defining $t$ has finite support. There is a nonzero effective exceptional divisor $Z$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-discrepancy} D=-Z,\qquad D^2<0,\qquad p_a(Z)=1. \end{equation} The map $C\to B_0$ is an isomorphism, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-image-class} D_A\equiv2\mathcal L \end{equation} numerically on $A$. Let $E_X$ be the norm divisor constructed in the proof; it is effective, has full exceptional support, and satisfies $2K_X\sim2C+E_X$. Then the actual divisor equality is \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-image-pullback} \alpha^*D_A=2C+E_X+2Z. \end{equation} The two defects satisfy \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-stein-defect} K_X^2=d+4t+Z^2,\qquad 2t=d+\epsilon. \end{equation} In particular $\epsilon$ is even. Moreover, \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-double-cover-line} \omega_{X_0}\simeq a_0^*\mathcal L,\qquad \mathcal L^2=2\bigl(\chi(\OO_X)+t\bigr) =\frac{3d}{2}+\epsilon, \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-image-cycle} C\cdot Z=d+2\epsilon,\qquad Z^2=-c_2(X)-2\epsilon. \end{equation} The exceptional intersection form gives \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-defect-tradeoff} 4c_2(X)t\ge d^2,\qquad t\ge\max\left\{\frac d2, \left\lceil\frac{d^2}{4c_2(X)}\right\rceil\right\}. \end{equation} Equivalently, $2c_2(X)(d+\epsilon)\ge d^2$. Equality in $4c_2(X)t\ge d^2$ holds precisely when \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-tradeoff-equality} (d-c_2(X))E_X=2c_2(X)Z \end{equation} as real exceptional divisors. The conditions $\epsilon=0$, $t=d/2$, and smoothness of $D'$ are equivalent; in that case $c_2(X)\ge d/2$. In particular $X_0$ has a nonrational singularity and $\alpha$ is not finite.

exact_statement_tex: [The smallest endpoint in Albanese degree two] \label{thm:smallest-endpoint-albanese-summary} Let $X$ be a smooth integral projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, and let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor. For $\epsilon=p_a(D')-g(Y)\ge0$, one has \[ D_A\equiv2\mathcal L,\qquad 2t=d+\epsilon,\qquad \mathcal L^2=\frac{3d}{2}+\epsilon. \] In particular $\epsilon$ is even, and \[ t\ge\max\left\{\frac d2, \left\lceil\frac{d^2}{4c_2(X)}\right\rceil\right\}. \] If $Y$ is very ample, then $4\mid d$, $d\ge16$, and \[ 6\le h^0(X,\OO_X(Y))\le d/4+2. \]

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:normalized-mup-conductor} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth ample integral curve, and let $M$ be a nontrivial line bundle of order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Choose a trivialization of $M^p$ and let $T\to X$ be its $\mu_p$-torsor. Let $N$ be the normalization of $T$ and $\pi:N\to X$ the resulting finite map. The logarithmic differential of $M$ has order $pa$ along $Y$ for an integer $a\geq1$, with nonzero tangential leading coefficient. The full inverse image $D=\pi^*Y$ is a reduced integral ample Cartier divisor. At its generic point the ramification index is one, the residue degree is $p$, and the conductor of $T$ in $N$ has coefficient $a(p-1)$. The normalization $\widetilde D$ of $D$ has genus $g(Y)$. Let $\mathfrak c\subset\OO_N$ be the conductor ideal, put $c=a(p-1)$, and set $\mathcal J=\mathfrak c\otimes\OO_N(cD)$. Then $\mathcal J$ is a reflexive ideal in $\OO_N$, and its restriction embeds in $\OO_D$ with finite-length quotient. Write $\ell$ for that length and put $\delta=p_a(D)-g(Y)$. Without any smoothness or Gorenstein assumption on $N$, one has \[ 2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2+\frac{\ell+2\delta}{p-1}, \qquad \ell\geq0,\quad\delta\geq0. \] If $2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2$, then $D$ is smooth, $N$ is regular near $D$, $\mathcal J=\OO_N$, and $N$ is Gorenstein. If $N$ is singular at a point of $D$, then $2g(Y)-2-apY^2\geq2/(p-1)$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{cor:normalized-equality-torsor} In the notation and hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}, suppose $2g(Y)-2=apY^2$. Let $L=\OO_X(aY)$ and let $s_a$ be its canonical section. Define $G_{s_a}$ by the formula in Corollary~\ref{cor:smooth-torsor}, with $L$ and $s_a$ in place of $\OO_X(Y)$ and $s$. Then $\pi:N\to X$ is a $G_{s_a}$-torsor. Its infinitesimal action is a homomorphism \[ \OO_N(-aD)\longrightarrow T_N \] that is nonzero on every fibre, is tangent to $D$, and restricts to an isomorphism $\OO_D(-aD)\simeq T_D$. If $a=1$, the surface $N$ has at least one singular point outside $D$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:normalized-mup-singularity-defect} Keep the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}, and suppose that \[ 2g(Y)-2=apY^2. \] Let $\omega$ be the logarithmic differential of $M$, put $m=pa$, and let $s_Y$ be the canonical section of $\OO_X(Y)$. The section \[ \theta=\omega/s_Y^m\in H^0\bigl(X,\Omega^1_{X/k}(-mY)\bigr) \] has a finite zero scheme $Z$ disjoint from $Y$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-mup-zero-length} \operatorname{length}_k Z=c_2(X)+apY^2=c_2(X)+aD^2. \end{equation} The singular subscheme of $N$ defined by $\operatorname{Fitt}_2(\Omega^1_{N/k})$ is $N\times_X Z$. Its length is $p\operatorname{length}_k Z$, and $N$ is smooth if and only if $Z$ is empty. The tangent sheaf $T_N$ is a vector bundle of rank two, even when $N$ is singular. The infinitesimal action of Corollary~\ref{cor:normalized-equality-torsor} gives an exact sequence of vector bundles \begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-mup-tangent-sequence} 0\longrightarrow\OO_N(-aD)\longrightarrow T_N \longrightarrow\omega_N^{-1}(aD)\longrightarrow0, \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\label{eq:normalized-mup-tangent-chern} \deg c_2(T_N)=-aD^2. \end{equation} If $a=1$, then $Z$ is nonempty, so $c_2(X)+pY^2\geq1$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:distinguished-ruled-cover} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor, and let $M\ne\OO_X$ have order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Let $N$ be the normalization of the $\mu_p$-torsor defined by a trivialization of $M^{\otimes p}$. If a ruled surface $R$ admits a dominant purely inseparable rational map of degree $p$ to $X$, then \[ k(R)=k(N)\quad\text{as extensions of }k(X). \] In particular $N$ is birationally ruled, and every smooth projective model of its function field has Kodaira dimension $-\infty$. A resolution of the rational map from a smooth projective ruled model gives a proper birational morphism to $N$ over $X$. The surface $X$ itself is not birationally ruled. Moreover, if $k(N)=A(t)$ is a ruling presentation, then \[ k(X)\cap A=A^p,\qquad k(X)A=k(N). \]

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:positive-genus-picard-fibration} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor, and let $M\ne\OO_X$ have order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Suppose that \[ 2g(Y)-2=pY^2. \] Let $\pi:N\to X$ be the normalization of the $\mu_p$-torsor defined by a trivialization of $M^p$, and put $D=\pi^*Y$. Assume that $N$ is birationally ruled, and fix a presentation \[ k(N)=k(C)(t) \] with $C$ a smooth projective integral curve of genus at least one. Put $B=C^{(p)}$, and denote relative Frobenius by $F_{C/k}:C\to B$. There are projective flat morphisms $f:X\to B$ and $h:N\to C$ such that \[ f\pi=F_{C/k}h, \] and $N$ is the normalization of the integral surface $X\times_B C$. The singularities of $N$ are rational double points. Moreover, \[ h_*\OO_N=\OO_C,\qquad R^ih_*\OO_N=0\quad(i>0), \qquad \chi(\OO_N)=1-g(C). \] There is a nonempty open subset $C_0\subset C$ over which $N_{C_0}\simeq C_0\times\PP^1$ as a $C_0$-scheme. For corresponding general closed points $c\in C$ and $b_0=F_{C/k}(c)\in B$, let $F_N=h^{-1}(c)$ and $F_X=f^{-1}(b_0)$. Then $F_X$ is integral and geometrically unibranch, and $\pi|_{F_N}:F_N\simeq\PP^1\to F_X$ is its finite radicial normalization. One has \[ \pi^*F_X=pF_N,\qquad \pi_*F_N=F_X. \] Writing $b=Y\cdot F_X=D\cdot F_N$, one obtains \[ 2p_a(F_X)=(p-1)b,\qquad b>0. \] In characteristic two, $b$ is even. In particular the general fibre $F_X$ is singular. If $Y$ is very ample, then $b\geq p+2$.

exact_statement_tex: [Universal range modulo algebraic equivalence]\label{thm:range} The following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For $0\leq i\leq n/2$, the map $L^{n-2i}:A^i(X)\to A^{n-i}(X)$ is surjective for every smooth projective complex $n$-fold and every ample $L$ if and only if $i=0$ or $2i=n$. For each $1\leq i<n/2$ there is an $X$ for which the source is finite-dimensional and the target infinite-dimensional, for every ample $L$. \item For $0\leq r\leq n$, each of the following properties holds for every such $n$-fold in codimension $r$ if and only if $r\in\{0,1,n\}$: injectivity of the rational cycle class map; coincidence of algebraic and numerical equivalence after tensoring with $\Q$; finite-dimensionality of $A^r(X)$; finite generation of $(\CH^r(X)/\CH^r(X)_{\alg})/\mathrm{torsion}$. \item If $n=2m$ and $P^m_L(X)=\ker(L:A^m(X)\to A^{m+1}(X))$, then \[ q(x,y)=(-1)^m\deg(xy) \] is positive semidefinite on $P^m_L(X)$ and \[ \rad(q)=\ker\bigl(L:G^m(X)\to G^{m+1}(X)\bigr). \] Thus positive definiteness is exactly the injectivity of this last map. It holds universally for $m=0,1$. No assertion for all $m\geq2$ follows from parts~(i) and~(ii). \end{enumerate}
